setlist.title: Beat It On Down the Line

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Scarlet Begonias** (2 reviews): Scarlet into Fire has a long, dreamy transition jam leading into an incendiary Fire; Reviewer says Garcia definitely takes Scarlet Begonias far out [5][14]
- **Not Fade Away** (2 reviews): Not Fade Away clearly segues into Wharf Rat; Drums lead into Not Fade Away, which then goes into Wharf Rat [5][6]
- **Eyes Of The World** (1 review): Reviewer vaguely recognized Eyes of the World at his first show [9]

## Setlist highlights

- **Deal X**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]

## The recordings

- **gd1978-12-22.161817.aud.keith.cotsman.sirmick.flac16** (recommended): audience recording; 18 songs; 129 min [1]. Said about its sound: Original is very bottom heavy and its vocals were low, especially in Set I; the remaster applies EQ, lifts vocals and trims arena reverb [1]
- **gd78-12-22.aud.cotsman.14562.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 17 songs; 129 min; rated 2.94/5 by 17 [2]. Said about its sound: Scarlet Begonias sounds distant, like the back of the room, and Garcia's playing is very hard to make out; Second set has cuts and imperfect quality, but remains very listenable; The tape cuts out at the end [3][5][6][14]

## Around the show

- A 16-year-old attended his first Dead show here; a funny account was published on the Dallas Observer blog [8]
- Reviewer attended as a first Dead show, disliking the town, hair and pot, but it started his fandom [9]
- Attendee recalls Around and Around near the end, possibly after Not Fade Away, though it appears on no recording or setlist [12]
- At the Fox, the band played Johnny B. Goode as an encore; the Summit may have had none [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1978-12-22.161817.aud.keith.cotsman.sirmick.flac16**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Sirmick, Jeff Cotsman, Chuck Kiefe; source: AUD > MC > ? > D > CD > EAC > SHN > wav [1]. Also: This is a remaster of shnid 14562, with azimuth adjusted and speed fluctuations corrected using Celemony Capstan, though some remain [1]
- **gd78-12-22.aud.cotsman.14562.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording [2]. Also: Lineage given as audience recording, then MC, an unknown generation, DAT, CD, EAC and SHN; Most of sets 1 and 2 came via Chuck Kiefe, with encoding by Jeff Cotsman; Reviewer says only Shakedown Street is missing from the tape, not the three songs the text file claims [2][4]
